verdict.rationale: Devin is itself the built-in AI assistant. Its docs describe delegating tickets, features, bug fixes and internal tools through a conversational interface with an embedded IDE, as well as through Slack/Teams tagging and Ask Devin. Hands-on community reports confirm users delegate real work to it, though they note it sometimes adds extraneous changes or gets stuck. missing for 10: independent corroboration that delegated tasks are completed reliably without close supervision.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Ask Devin to tackle Linear/Jira tickets, implement entirely new features, repro and fix bugs, build internal tools, and more!
Devin is designed to be a conversational user interface, and allows you to follow and take over Devin's development process in the embedded IDE.
Tagging Devin on a Slack or Teams thread about a bug you're discussing with coworkers
I've managed to get real work done out of it without much effort, just checking every 10-15 minutes and typing a few lines or restarting session.
